newsitem.title: USA: NYCE cotton called to open flat to down 0.10 cent.
newsitem.headline: NYCE cotton called to open flat to down 0.10 cent.

text.p: NYCE cotton futures were called to open unchanged to 0.10 cent weaker Monday, based on market orders at 1017 EDT, traders said.

Prices are expected to consolidate gains made Friday, when most-active July ended 1.05 cents higher at 73.49 cents a lb after trading from 73.70 to 73.00 cents, where support was pegged. Spot May closed up 1.23 cents at 71.88 cents.
Volume was estimated at a moderate 10,000 lots.
Analysts said prices could ultimately climb to 76.50 basis July. Support was pegged at 73.00 cents.
In fundamental news, traders in Hong Kong said that China's Cotton and Jute Corp was offering cotton to domestic mills at discounted prices, in order to liquidate stocks.

South American countries will import an estimated 600,000 tonnes of cotton in 1996/97, a record for the region and 11 percent of world trade, the International Cotton Advisory Council said. The Western Hemisphere receives one-fourth of U.S. exports and nearly all of Argentina's exports, ICAC said.
In Texas, cold wet weather continues to delay planting. Several farmers will switch to other crops since it is now too late to plant cotton in some areas.
